Immortal: Unchained. The title sums up the story and lore of the game - they are generic and boring. Just some words that fill up some space... 

Luckily that is not the most important part. It is fun to explore the interconnected levels and looting everything. There are a lot of various weapons to find including unusual pieces like a sniper rifle with a flamethrower attachment or a shotgun with a big shield around its barrel. 

The game is far from perfect but you can have some solid fun and replayability for a really good price.
A bit rough at the start but gets better once you get more equipment
Imagine a game where enemies spawn behind your back and kill you with one shot! Do not waste your money even if you are hardcore souls games player like me.

I saw some comparison with Dark Souls. I haven't played that one. But from my perspective this was a good game. Here is my experience with it: 
   Slow starter this one. Initially I thought I had to play same few arenas over and over.  Till I was 10+ hours deep, I was curious as to why I play this game. The enemies were difficult, ammo was limited. Though you can always use ammo packs, I don't prefer this approach since I don't know when I will really need them. When you go to spawn points the enemies reanimated, same difficulties over and over again. 
   Then I realized I need a pretty good melee weapon. Found one, invested in it a lot. Started to save ammo and I was able to reach other checkpoints relatively easy. 
   But again going deep in the scenario and then coming back just to reach to the beginning was both boring and troublesome. That lasted till you connect the network. Then everything began to shape in a different feeling. The connections of the levels to different places become interesting and enjoyable. My character got strong enough to use good weapons. Along with the 3rd and 4th weapon slots unlocked I had good amount of ammo to use. I mastered the most important skills. Even the boss fights became more manageable. 
Completing the game and starting over again I think the level design is good. Once you learn the attack types of enemies fights are enjoyable. 
   Heads up though, this is not kind of hack-n-slash type FPS. There is no horde of enemies you will carelessly start shooting. Sometimes fighting a single enemy requires tactics.

Ok, bought this game on sale and wasn't expecting much, but actually found it quite enjoyable. But its a labor of love. And don't get me wrong is real rough around the edges at times, but the core of it is pretty fun. 

They nailed the tone and vibe of this game, which in essence, is like a Chronicles of Riddick in The Matrix kinda world. It's a dark and gritty digital world that frankly looks great for the most part. They made this a souls-like difficult game, that's mainly focused around the gun-play and makes it fun. I think if they fixed a few things, and refined a few more, a second title of this could be really great. But for now, its a flawed game with good potential.

If you're a souls-like fan, give this thing a try!

This game is quite fun! Is there a bit of jank and clunk? Oh yeah definitely! Here's the ups and downs:

Ups:
-Has an awesome atmosphere set through the world/level design, character/enemy design, soundtrack! 
-Loved the variety of weapons and secondary attacks! Mainly used the shottys (as secondary weapon, the primary ones were meh) and sniper rifle with occasional assault rifle. Not sure why anyone would use a pistol and didn't really experiment with SMGs. Played with the launchers a bit but with my stat build couldn't really use em.
-More of a coherent story than Dark Souls or Elden Ring XD (but who really plays souls-like for the story?) That ending though! ROFL
-Gameplay is fun and smooth! Boss fights were cool, mostly not too difficult (final boss was EZ, 1st try).
-Useful items!!! Reusable (or replenishable whichever) grenades!!! (OMG the grenades are too good) Run out of ammo? Use an ammo pack, you get PLENTY!
-Armor Shrines! Rather than having to worry about equipment weight and what armor to equip, you get free permanent upgrades at armor shrines! AND THEY ARE GOOD UPGRADES!!!
-All stat upgrades you can level actually seemed useful and impactful!
-Abundance of loot! You also get plenty of resources to upgrade weapons so you don't have to be too careful with how you spend you them! Upgrade away!
-Really cool how you can stagger enemies and even destroy their limbs so they can't hold a gun anymore or have to crawl towards you!

Downs (more of a heads up than a warning):
-The stat requirements for a lot of the better weapons seemed a bit high so you had to level quite a bit into one or two stats before you could use them (which essentially made using another type of weapon inaccessible, in all fairness you do get 1 Respec Core, but I was worried about messing up my respec if I didn't like how using other weapons worked).
-There was one area, the graveyard area, which the game crashed multiple times, I ended having to replay that segment way too many times. I thought it was going to be unplayable at that point but I did the ole "Verify Integrity of Files" Steam trick and seemed to help enough to get out of that area then it didn't really happen anywhere else.
-If you die, good luck trying to run back to your bits (souls), as you will most likely have to kill every enemy again on the way back to where you died (which isn't completely terrible, but can make it a bit more tedious than I'd prefer).
-There were so many loot chests that were set up to backtrack for since you didn't have enough of the required items to open when you first pass them. But as to my last point you most likely would have to kill every enemy to get back to it if you could even remember where the chests are (occasionally there were some that the game paths you back to so it was a nice surprise to be like "Ooooo I can open this now!").
-The fast travel >_< having to spend 5k bits to unlock fast travel at each shrine was a bit annoying (especially since by the time you unlock this feature you're about halfway through the game). Should let you just fast travel to any shrine you've been too or at least be able to buy the fast travels at each shrine from the start.
-As an extension of the last point, after the Holmeguard Commander Boss (2nd boss in the game) you feel like you hit a dead end since no paths unlock, no dialogue about where you need to go next. But what the game wants you to do is backtrack through the whole level you just went through. Sure there are some shortcuts you unlock but you still gotta kill mostly every enemy on the way out (again not too terrible but still a bit tedious). This would have been a perfect opportunity to introduce fast travel at the very least!
-F'ing teleporting enemies with the shotgun. One was enough of a pain to deal with but if you go into an area too fast and spawn in a second or third? Ya ded.
-Some of the distances between save shrines were looooooooooong, holy heck! Wasn't too frequent they did that but my word, the game got me so paranoid about dying and losing so much progress (since running past enemies is almost never an option)
-I wish melee was more useful as most enemies in the game are ranged. Occasionally there were a few good uses for melee like breaking through those damn portable shields enemies drop that you can't shoot through or for some of the teleporting enemies to get a quick attack in before they get a shot off on you. But overall melee was a bit underwhelming, 

So while it looks like there's more down than up based on the above, it's not. This game has got so much awesome to it, that it is worth playing in my opinion! You just have to go in with an open mind and let it be it's own game! Yes some things will be a bit more tedious than one would prefer, but a few attempts and you'll get through it. You'll get a feel and rhythm for the game rather quickly. It is a difficult game mostly from navigating the levels with a lot of enemies in the path. You just got to be cautious and strategic about approaching certain situations because if you try going in guns blazing or running past.... ya ded.

I had more fun with this game than Dark Souls 3 and Elden Ring, so....Would recommend! :)

It's like a slightly janky clunky less polished older sibling to Remnant From the Ashes! (I LOVED THAT GAME!!)

And it's only $11!!!! Fantastic value even if you pay full price! (But you know...get it on sale, obviously) So get it! ;)

Well this is another of those cases that i wish steam had a "Neutral" review option.

The good:
-Cool graphics
-Good amount of weapons and weapon types(even if some of them are pretty useless)
-Good amout of stats and build possibilties
-Overall cool map design(except for the last 2 maps, i will detail later)
-Amazing map exploration, the game really wants you to explore every corner of it.
-The story is pretty cool and the ending is really unexpected(wont spoil anything)

The neutral:
-The combat if a little clunky, but honestly it is easy to adapt 
-As i mentioned before, there are some types of weapons that are so weak that dont even make sense, pistols and smgs
-Some enemies are pretty bad designed, it would need to have some improvements.
-The game have some balance problems, most on the weapons side, some weapons felt too OP and some too useless

The bad:
-As i mentioned before the 2 last maps felt REALLY uninspired and boring, there was sometimes that i was asking myself, "why i am still playing this?"
-It has some performance issues, i have a 10700k overclocked and a 3070 and sometimes my game was running at 40 fps
-The beginning of the game felt WAY harder than the ending, probably because you have better equips and etc, but i feel like it should be the opposite, as you get stronger the game should be harder, not easier.
-The bosses of this game are the worst, they are boring, easy and pretty dissapointing

I am letting a positive review because the game got a huge price cut, and right now is really cheap, for the price asked now i really think that it worth it, if you want something different and like difficult games, you will probably like this.
